counterfactual_missing_items: Pancreatic head biopsy: Hypocellular with scant atypical cells
BiliSeq genetic sequencing: Demonstrated genomic alterations in targeted regions of genes involved in biliary-tract malignancies
decisive_items: Biliary stricture biopsy: Consistent with adenocarcinoma
CT abdomen/pelvis: 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation, without evidence of metastatic disease
response.rationale: R4 best integrates the pancreatic head mass, pancreatic ductal dilatation, obstructive jaundice, and adenocarcinoma on biliary stricture biopsy into one unifying pancreatic neoplasm. R3 shares the malignant biliary/pancreaticobiliary evidence but lacks the pancreatic primary anatomy and is therefore less complete. R1 and R2 explain the muscle/rhabdomyolysis findings as complications or coincidental features but cannot account for the pancreaticobiliary malignancy.

rejected.why: CK elevation and biceps biopsy support rhabdomyolysis, but this is a secondary complication and does not explain the pancreatic head mass, biliary adenocarcinoma, or obstructive jaundice.
Atorvastatin exposure plus elevated CK is only correlative; there is no raw causal link to statin myopathy, and it does not explain the pancreaticobiliary malignancy.
